title: Raw coefficient refinements and their explicit comparison maps
statement:
Let $S$ be a qcqs scheme with the selected finite affine gluing presentation $\mathsf G_S$ of [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation]. Write $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ for its main charts. Keep the presentation's finite lists of principal opens $D_{A_a}(f_p)$ covering each overlap, in both orientations. Each such piece $p:a\to b$ has the fixed original map into $U_b$, hence a ring map $\rho_p:A_b\to(A_a)_{f_p}$. These maps are restrictions of the overlap identifications of this one scheme, not arbitrary endomorphisms. Localizations mean [def-weil-ring-localization-away].
Fix a raw coefficient tuple $C=(C_a)_a$: each $C_a\subseteq A_a$ is a subring generated by finitely many elements over $\mathbf Z$, contains every labelled $f_p$ on that chart, and satisfies $\rho_p(C_b)\subseteq(C_a)_{f_p}$, inside $(A_a)_{f_p}$. Retain the resulting restricted maps $\rho_{p,C}:C_b\to(C_a)_{f_p}$. This is the precise raw coefficient input; no open-preservation or gluing equations are required of it.
Define $I(C)$ to be the set of all tuples $B=(B_a)_a$ of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subrings $C_a\subseteq B_a\subseteq A_a$ satisfying $\rho_p(B_b)\subseteq(B_a)_{f_p}$ for every labelled piece. Order it by componentwise inclusion. Regard this preorder as a thin category: a morphism $B\to B'$ is the condition $B\leq B'$, with identity and composition given by reflexivity and transitivity. The ring diagram on chart $a$ sends $B$ to $B_a$ and a morphism to inclusion $j^a_{BB'}$. The raw datum at $B$ consists of $X_{a,B}=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$, the pieces $P_{p,B}=\operatorname{Spec}(B_a)_{f_p}$ with their principal-open inclusions into $X_{a,B}$, their unions $W_{ab,B}$, and the maps $p_B:P_{p,B}\to X_{b,B}$ induced by the restrictions $\rho_{p,B}$; the reverse-orientation pieces give the proposed reverse maps. The spectrum convention is [def-weil-affine-spectrum].
For $B\leq B'$ the localized transition is explicitly
$$j^{a,f}_{BB'}:(B_a)_f\longrightarrow(B'_a)_f,\qquad x/f^n\longmapsto j^a_{BB'}(x)/f^n.$$
The chart comparison is $q^a_{B'B}=\operatorname{Spec}(j^a_{BB'})$, and the piece comparison is the spectrum of $j^{a,f_p}_{BB'}$. The square defining $P_{p,B'}\to P_{p,B}$ is the inverse-image square for $D(f_p)$ under $q^a_{B'B}$, in the sense of the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]: a morphism into $X_{a,B'}$ factors through this piece exactly when the image of $f_p$ is invertible. The identification of $\operatorname{Spec}(B_a)_{f_p}$ with the principal open uses [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. The restricted maps obey
$$j^{a,f_p}_{BB'}\rho_{p,B}=\rho_{p,B'}j^b_{BB'}.$$
This equation specifies the comparison of overlap maps. It is not an assertion that every square between two different chart indices is Cartesian. The raw datum refined from $C$ to $B$ means this explicitly defined datum at $B$ and these comparison maps, not an unspecified tensor extension of a map between independently enlarged rings.
Restrictions and composite maps are formed on their actual domains. For example, if $p:a\to b$, $q:b\to d$, and $\rho_{p,B}(f_q)=h/f_p^n$, the domain of $q_Bp_B$ is $D(f_ph)\subseteq X_{a,B}$, with coordinate ring $(B_a)_{f_ph}$. Domains for comparing two paths are intersections of their domains, so products of the corresponding principal-open elements. Unions use the finite lists of pieces, retaining the agreement conditions on intersections. All these domain elements and any chosen fraction representatives are retained when the corresponding finite test is formed. Their later comparison maps use the same fraction formula. The equality and inverse-image formulas are the meaning of transport in this construction. This definition selects neither a valid gluing stage nor a glued scheme.
